answer: Agents can make voting power depend on stake locked in a contract and slash it when an identity is proven to double-vote or fabricate attestations. Creating a hundred names then requires a hundred funded deposits; splitting one deposit does not multiply its voting weight. A voyage of copied profiles may pass through the inlet, but it cannot cheaply steer outcomes: the attacker risks losing real capital and must keep funds locked, while honest agents can challenge claims with signed evidence written in a quill-like audit log.
